In [[knot theory]], '''Willerton's fish''' is an unexplained relationship between the first two [[Vassiliev invariant]]s of a [[knot (mathematics)|knot]]. These invariants are {{math|''c''<sub>2</sub>}}, the quadratic [[coefficient]] of the [[Alexander–Conway polynomial]], and {{math|''j''<sub>3</sub>}}, an order-three invariant derived from the [[Jones polynomial]].<ref name="cdm">{{citation
 | last1 = Chmutov | first1 = S.
 | last2 = Duzhin | first2 = S.
 | last3 = Mostovoy | first3 = J.
 | contribution = 14.3 Willerton's fish and bounds for {{math|''c''<sub>2</sub>}} and {{math|''j''<sub>3</sub>}}
 | contribution-url = https://books.google.com/books?id=HCNB0yV09TsC&pg=PA419
 | doi = 10.1017/CBO9781139107846
 | isbn = 978-1-107-02083-2
 | mr = 2962302
 | pages = 419–420
 | publisher = Cambridge University Press, Cambridge
 | title = Introduction to Vassiliev knot invariants
 | url = http://www.pdmi.ras.ru/~duzhin/papers/cdbook/cdbook.pdf
 | year = 2012| arxiv = 1103.5628
 }}.</ref><ref name="dss">{{citation
 | last1 = Dunin-Barkowski | first1 = P.
 | last2 = Sleptsov | first2 = A.
 | last3 = Smirnov | first3 = A.
 | arxiv = 1112.5406
 | doi = 10.1142/S0217751X13300251
 | issue = 17
 | journal = International Journal of Modern Physics A
 | mr = 3081407
 | page = 1330025
 | title = Kontsevich integral for knots and Vassiliev invariants
 | volume = 28
 | year = 2013| bibcode = 2013IJMPA..2830025D}}. See in particular Section 4.2.1, "Willerton's fish and families of knots".</ref>

When the values of {{math|''c''<sub>2</sub>}} and {{math|''j''<sub>3</sub>}}, for knots of a given fixed [[Crossing number (knot theory)|crossing number]], are used as the {{mvar|x}} and {{mvar|y}} coordinates of a [[scatter plot]], the points of the plot appear to fill a fish-shaped region of the plane, with a lobed body and two sharp tail fins. The region appears to be bounded by [[cubic curve]]s,<ref name="dss"/> suggesting that the crossing number, {{math|''c''<sub>2</sub>}}, and {{math|''j''<sub>3</sub>}} may be related to each other by not-yet-proven [[Inequality (mathematics)|inequalities]].<ref name="cdm"/>

This shape is named after Simon Willerton,<ref name="cdm"/> who first observed this phenomenon and described the shape of the scatterplots as "fish-like".<ref>{{citation
 | last = Willerton | first = Simon
 | issue = 2
 | journal = [[Experimental Mathematics (journal)|Experimental Mathematics]]
 | mr = 1959269
 | pages = 289–296
 | title = On the first two Vassiliev invariants
 | url = http://projecteuclid.org/euclid.em/1062621221
 | volume = 11
 | year = 2002
 | doi = 10.1080/10586458.2002.10504692
 }}.</ref>
